subject: English
passage: The House of Mirth is a 1905 novel by Edith Wharton set in New York City at the turn of the century. In the novel, Lily Bart attends a society gathering. Lily compares her intellect favorably to that of other women of New York City society who are in attendance: ______
prompt: Which quotation from The House of Mirth best illustrates the claim?

choices.A: "Singly [the women around Lily] betrayed their superficiality; but grouped together they represented 'Society,' and the habit of feminine conformity made her accept their doctrine on all matters of taste."
choices.B: "Lily Bart, reclining on the settee near the window [where her place was], turned her eyes from the garden and surveyed the opposite end of the drawing room."
choices.C: "Lily Bart felt herself distinctly the superior of these chosen specimens of old New York aristocracy; she had probably traveled more, experienced more, and even understood a good deal more of the world, than any other woman of the gathering."
choices.D: "To arrive at the dinner party in a [hired carriage] was almost as respectable a way of arriving as in one's own private coach."

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it directly illustrates the claim that Lily compares her intellect favorably to that of other women in New York society. The quotation explicitly states that 'Lily Bart felt herself distinctly the superior of these chosen specimens' and provides the basis for this comparison: 'she had probably traveled more, experienced more, and even understood a good deal more of the world, than any other woman of the gathering.' This directly demonstrates Lily viewing her own knowledge and experience as exceeding that of the other society women present.
